Issue Title: General MPS op coverage tracking issue
Requirement: The PyTorch project shall include a comprehensive mechanism for tracking and reporting the coverage of Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) operators. This feature must provide clear visibility into which MPS ops are currently supported, identify gaps, and facilitate prioritization for future implementation, ensuring full indexable integration and maintenance of MPS backend compatibility.

Issue Title: ARM Mac 16-core Neural Engine
Requirement: Requirement: Extend the PyTorch framework to support execution on ARM-based Macs utilizing the built-in 16-core Neural Engine for accelerated neural network computations.

Issue Title: PyPy support
Requirement: The system MUST support the PyPy interpreter, ensuring that all primary PyTorch functionality is compatible with and runnable under a current stable release of PyPy.

Issue Title: Implement similar PyTorch function as model.summary() in keras?
Requirement: The system shall provide a function that generates a detailed summary of a PyTorch model's architecture, including layer types, output shapes, parameter counts, and memory usage, similar to Keras' model.summary() functionality.

Issue Title: CPU version of PyTorch on PyPI
Requirement: The system MUST provide a CPU-only version of PyTorch available for installation via PyPI, ensuring that users who do not have GPU support can easily install and use PyTorch without unnecessary dependencies.

Issue Title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
Requirement: Implement a function in PyTorch's random module that replicates the behavior of numpy.random.choice, supporting selection from a 1-D tensor or range of integers with options for sampling with or without replacement, probability weights, and multidimensional output.

Issue Title: [RFC] Add tar-based IterableDataset implementation to PyTorch
Requirement: Implement a tar-based IterableDataset in PyTorch that reads data directly from tar archives without extracting the contents, providing support for streaming data and parallel processing where applicable.

Issue Title: [Feature request] Let DistributedSampler take a Sampler as input
Requirement: The DistributedSampler module must be enhanced to accept an optional Sampler instance as input, allowing users to integrate custom sampling strategies while preserving existing functionality and ensuring proper data distribution across processes.

Issue Title: [FYI] NestedTensor Project Progress
Requirement: Implement a NestedTensor abstraction in PyTorch that allows for efficient and memory-safe operations on collections of tensors with variable sizes. This feature should seamlessly integrate with the existing PyTorch API, support common tensor operations (including indexing, slicing, and batching), and provide performance optimizations over traditional padded tensor approaches for handling irregular data structures.

Issue Title: [Proposal] Data reading framework for PyTorch (Hive, MySQL, S3 etc.)
Requirement: Implement a data reading framework for PyTorch that provides a unified API for connecting to and reading data from various sources such as Hive, MySQL, and S3. The framework must be extensible, support efficient data ingestion and transformation pipelines, and integrate seamlessly with standard PyTorch data processing workflows.

Issue Title: Statically checked tensor shapes
Requirement: The system shall provide support for statically checked tensor shapes by allowing developers to specify shape annotations for tensors in function signatures. The feature must integrate with Python type annotations and offer compile-time or lint-time verification of tensor shape compatibility to catch mismatches before runtime, ensuring that tensor operations are executed only when their dimensional requirements are met.

Issue Title: [RFC] DataLoader architecture updates and TarDataset implementation
Requirement: The system shall update the DataLoader architecture to support enhanced data streaming and parallelism, and introduce a TarDataset implementation that enables efficient iteration over tarball archives as datasets.

Issue Title: Transformer Lack of Embedding Layer and Positional Encodings
Requirement: The Transformer module in PyTorch should include built-in support for an embedding layer and positional encodings, allowing users to seamlessly integrate these components into the model architecture without requiring external implementations.

Issue Title: [RFC] TorchStore - A Shared-Memory Tensor Store
Requirement: Implement a shared-memory tensor store for PyTorch ("TorchStore") that supports high-performance creation, retrieval, and deletion of tensors across multiple processes. The tensor store should efficiently manage shared memory, ensure concurrency safety, and provide a clear API for integration into PyTorch workflows.

Issue Title: [FR][RFC] Build a serving framework to host and serve trained PyTorch models
Requirement: The software shall include a serving framework that allows users to host and serve trained PyTorch models efficiently. The framework must provide a straightforward API for deploying models, handling incoming inference requests, and managing resource allocation. It should support common deployment scenarios, including RESTful endpoints and batch processing, and be extensible to accommodate custom model serving pipelines and configurations.

Issue Title: [RFC] DeepSpeed + PT Distributed Integration
Requirement: Integrate DeepSpeed's advanced distributed training capabilities with PyTorch's native distributed framework, providing seamless interoperability between the two systems. The integration must support DeepSpeed's memory optimizations and performance enhancements within the PyTorch ecosystem, include comprehensive APIs for configuring distributed training settings, and come with clear documentation and compatibility assurances across different environments.

Issue Title: Parallel Associative Scan
Requirement: The PyTorch library shall include a parallel associative scan operator that performs prefix-sum computations over tensors using user-defined associative binary operations. The operator must support execution on both CPU and GPU, integrate with PyTorch's automatic differentiation framework, and be applicable to multi-dimensional tensors with optional batch dimensions.

Issue Title: Support for `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64`
Requirement: The system must support unsigned integer types uint16, uint32, and uint64, allowing operations, storage, and computations analogous to other numeric types in PyTorch.

Issue Title: Feature request: INT4 format support
Requirement: The software shall include native support for the INT4 format, allowing users to utilize INT4 precision in tensor operations, inference, and training within the PyTorch framework, ensuring compatibility with existing APIs and efficient utilization of hardware resources.

Issue Title: [feature request] Simple and Efficient way to get gradients of each element of a sum
Requirement: The system shall provide an API to efficiently compute and return the gradient for each individual element that contributes to a sum operation. This API should work seamlessly with existing tensor operations and automatic differentiation tools to offer a simple, direct method to inspect the per-element gradients of a summed tensor.

Issue Title: non-negative least squares solver feature request
Requirement: The software shall include a non-negative least squares (NNLS) solver within the PyTorch library that efficiently computes solutions to least squares problems while enforcing non-negativity constraints on the solution variables.

Issue Title: [RFC] RPC Based Distributed Model Parallel
Requirement: The system MUST support a distributed model parallelism framework based on RPC, enabling models to be partitioned across multiple nodes with transparent inter-node communication, asynchronous execution, error handling, and integration with PyTorch's existing distributed framework.

Issue Title: [Poll] Support DistributedDataParallel (DDP) in PyTorch C++ API (libtorch)
Requirement: Implement support for DistributedDataParallel (DDP) functionality in the PyTorch C++ API (libtorch), enabling multi-process distributed training with features and performance comparable to the Python API.

Issue Title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes
Requirement: The DataLoader should be enhanced with a configuration option that allows worker processes to be reused across multiple data loading iterations. This option must enable persistent worker processes to reduce the overhead of repeatedly spawning and terminating workers during training, while ensuring that data is correctly and efficiently loaded and that resources are managed safely across epochs.

Issue Title: [RFC] PT2-Friendly Traceable, Functional Collective Communication APIs
Requirement: The system shall provide a set of traceable, functional collective communication APIs designed for PT2 compatibility. These APIs must support core collective operations (e.g., allreduce, broadcast, gather, scatter) with built‐in traceability for debugging and performance analysis, integrate seamlessly with the existing PyTorch backend, and adhere to best practices for functional programming.

Issue Title: [feature request] Global GPU Flag
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a global GPU flag within the PyTorch framework that allows users to enable or disable GPU acceleration across all modules and operations. When set, this flag should uniformly affect device selection for computation, provide clear and consistent behavior for users, and integrate seamlessly with existing GPU configuration settings without adversely impacting backward compatibility.

Issue Title: OpenCL 3.0 support: support every GPU on earth through rusticl
Requirement: The system shall be enhanced to support OpenCL 3.0, enabling the use of RustICL for greater GPU compatibility. This feature must allow PyTorch to run on a wider range of GPUs, ensuring broad and efficient hardware utilization across available devices.

Issue Title: Zero-copy on shared memory of NVIDIA Jetson devices
Requirement: Implement a zero-copy mechanism for shared memory on NVIDIA Jetson devices, enabling efficient data handling without additional memory copy overhead for improved performance in PyTorch.

Issue Title: Feature Request: Easier to extend base RNN implementation
Requirement: The software shall be modified to provide a more extensible base RNN implementation that simplifies the creation of custom RNN modules. This includes designing clear abstraction layers, providing well-documented extension points, and ensuring that users can easily override or extend core functionalities without complex workarounds.

Issue Title: Return attention weights in nn.Transformer
Requirement: The Transformer module in nn.Transformer must include an option to return the attention weights computed during the multi-head attention operation, ensuring backward compatibility and clear API documentation for users.

Issue Title: Code Push / Hot Update / out of band updates
Requirement: The Flutter framework MUST provide built-in support for delivering code updates to deployed applications without requiring full app store releases. This feature shall enable developers to push hot updates or out-of-band patches—such as bug fixes or minor enhancements—to production apps, ensuring safe and seamless integration while maintaining compliance with platform policies and preserving application stability.

Issue Title: Enable "hot reload" (not just "hot restart") for Flutter Web
Requirement: The web implementation of Flutter must be enhanced to support hot reload functionality in addition to the existing hot restart, enabling developers to apply code changes in real time without a full restart of the application.

Issue Title: Let flutter be installable via homebrew
Requirement: The Flutter SDK should be made installable via Homebrew, allowing users to easily install, update, and manage Flutter through Homebrew commands on macOS systems.

Issue Title: Improve the indexability (SEO) of Flutter apps on the web
Requirement: The software shall improve the search engine optimization of Flutter web applications by implementing features that generate appropriate semantic HTML and dynamic meta tags, support progressive enhancement, and conform to industry best practices for web crawlers, ensuring that content indexability is maximized to enhance discoverability.

Issue Title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
Requirement: The software shall support multiple windows on desktop platforms, enabling users to open, close, and manage several independent windows concurrently within the application.

Issue Title: Implement PlatformView support on macOS
Requirement: The system MUST support PlatformView on macOS, enabling Flutter applications to embed and interact with native macOS views, consistent with the functionality provided on other supported platforms.

Issue Title: Server-side rendering for Flutter web
Requirement: The system shall enable server-side rendering for Flutter web applications, allowing developers to generate initial HTML content on the server to improve performance and SEO while maintaining full client-side interactivity.

Issue Title: Apple CarPlay / Android Auto support?
Requirement: The Flutter framework shall include support for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, enabling developers to build automotive applications with native integration into these in-car infotainment systems. This support must provide APIs and guidelines for handling display, input controls, and connectivity features specific to automotive environments.

Issue Title: [google_maps_flutter] Support Widgets as markers
Requirement: The google_maps_flutter plugin MUST allow developers to use Flutter widgets as custom marker icons, enabling dynamic and interactive rendering of markers on the map.

Issue Title: Implement PlatformView support on Windows
Requirement: The software shall implement PlatformView support on the Windows platform, enabling developers to embed native Windows UI components within Flutter applications.

Issue Title: Customizable project structure (platforms)
Requirement: The Flutter project scaffolding shall provide an option to customize the project structure for platform-specific components. This feature will allow developers to define customizable locations, names, and nesting of platform directories and resources without compromising backward compatibility with existing projects.

Issue Title: Add support for visionOS
Requirement: The Flutter framework shall include native support for visionOS, enabling developers to build, run, and deploy Flutter applications on visionOS devices. This support must include proper integration with visionOS-specific APIs for rendering, input, hardware interaction, and window management, in accordance with Apple's visionOS guidelines and best practices.

Issue Title: [web] Support compute on separate thread in Flutter Web
Requirement: The web engine must support running compute-intensive tasks on a separate thread in Flutter Web, analogous to the compute function available on mobile platforms, to improve performance and responsiveness.

Issue Title: Support home and lock screen widgets
Requirement: The Flutter framework shall support the creation and integration of home screen and lock screen widgets, enabling developers to build customizable, interactive widgets that seamlessly integrate with the native user experience on supported platforms.

Issue Title: [webview_flutter] Add Windows support
Requirement: The webview_flutter package MUST support the Windows platform by providing a fully functional WebView widget implementation that integrates smoothly with Flutter, including native UI rendering, input handling, and platform-specific APIs, ensuring parity in features and performance with existing implementations on iOS and Android.

Issue Title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
Requirement: The framework SHALL support soft hyphenation by recognizing the Unicode character U+00AD as an optional line break point and rendering an appropriate hyphen character at the end of the line when a break occurs.

Issue Title: Reusing state logic is either too verbose or too difficult
Requirement: The system MUST include a mechanism that simplifies the reuse of state logic, minimizing verbosity and reducing complexity in implementation.

Issue Title: Table > TableRow > TableCell colspan
Requirement: The Table widget must be enhanced to support a "colspan" property for TableCells, allowing individual cells to span multiple columns within a TableRow. This feature should include proper layout calculations and rendering adjustments to ensure accurate display and responsiveness in various table configurations.

Issue Title: Expo like tool for flutter
Requirement: The system shall provide an Expo-like development tool for Flutter that streamlines app initialization, configuration, development, and deployment. This tool must include features such as a built-in development server with live reload, simplified asset management, and an easy-to-use interface for building and deploying Flutter applications, while ensuring seamless integration with the existing Flutter ecosystem.

Issue Title: Flutter support for Apple Watch
Requirement: The Flutter framework shall provide native support for developing and deploying applications on Apple Watch, including the necessary tooling, templates, and performance optimizations to build, test, and integrate watchOS apps within existing Flutter projects.

Issue Title: [path_provider] Add support for web
Requirement: The path_provider package MUST be extended to include web support that provides equivalent file system functionality and API consistency with existing mobile platforms. The implementation should handle storing and retrieving files or data in an appropriate web environment, ensuring compatibility with common web browsers and adherence to web security practices.

Issue Title: SliverAppBar flexibleSpace with height depending on children
Requirement: The Flutter framework must support a dynamic SliverAppBar flexibleSpace area where the overall height is automatically calculated based on the dimensions of its child widgets, allowing for greater flexibility and adaptability in layout design.

Issue Title: Allow Hero widgets to have transitions within the same screen
Requirement: The system MUST support Hero widget transitions within the same screen, enabling smooth animations for widget transformations without requiring navigation to a different screen.

Issue Title: Investigate Swift Package Manager for Swift plugins
Requirement: Requirement: Investigate the feasibility and integration process of using the Swift Package Manager for managing and distributing Swift plugins within the Flutter framework. The evaluation should cover potential benefits, compatibility with existing project setups, and any necessary modifications or tooling updates needed for adoption.

Issue Title: Return index of the first visible item in ListView
Requirement: The software shall provide a method to determine and return the index of the first fully or partially visible item in a ListView, accurately reflecting the current scroll position.

Issue Title: Support Firefox as a browser in flutter run
Requirement: The Flutter tool must support launching and running web applications in the Firefox browser via the "flutter run" command, similar to existing support for other browsers.

Issue Title: [video_player] Support DRM content
Requirement: The video_player plugin MUST be enhanced to support DRM-protected content by integrating standard DRM systems (such as Widevine and PlayReady), including license acquisition and content decryption, while ensuring cross-platform compatibility and robust error handling.

Issue Title: [Desktop] - Splash screen or background color customization
Requirement: The desktop framework must provide developers with an option to customize the splash screen appearance or set a custom background color during application launch.

Issue Title: AVIF codec support
Requirement: The Flutter framework shall support decoding, rendering, and displaying images in the AVIF format, including full integration with the existing image pipeline and compatibility with popular platforms.

Issue Title: Allow release mode builds to run on simulators
Requirement: The flutter tool shall support building and running release mode builds on simulators, enabling developers to test release build behavior in simulated environments without device-specific restrictions.

Issue Title: Add structs in GDScript
Requirement: The system shall support the definition and use of structs in GDScript, allowing users to create custom composite data types with a fixed layout that can be used to group related data fields.

Issue Title: Add support for nullable static types in GDScript
Requirement: The software shall support nullable static types in GDScript, enabling developers to explicitly denote that a variable's type may accept a null value. This feature must integrate seamlessly with the existing static type system, maintaining type-safety while offering improved syntax for declaring nullable types.

Issue Title: Add a Trait system for GDScript
Requirement: GDScript shall include a trait system that enables code reuse across classes, allowing modules of reusable behavior to be defined independently and composed into different classes, thereby facilitating a more flexible alternative to traditional multiple inheritance.

Issue Title: Allow explicitly defining interfaces in GDScript
Requirement: GDScript must support explicit interface definitions that allow developers to declare interfaces with specified methods (and properties where applicable) to be implemented by other classes, providing compile-time checks and documentation consistent with object-oriented design principles.

Issue Title: Create a Swarm/Mob/Flock/etc system for managing large amounts of entities
Requirement: The system shall enable efficient management and simulation of large groups of entities using swarm, flock, or mob behaviors. It must provide customizable parameters for collective movement (such as cohesion, separation, and alignment) while ensuring high performance and seamless integration with existing simulation and game objects.

Issue Title: Expose a zero allocation API to Godot C# bindings
Requirement: The system shall provide a zero-allocation API for Godot's C# bindings to enable performance-critical operations without incurring garbage collection overhead, thereby reducing runtime memory allocations in performance-sensitive scenarios.

Issue Title: Add a "Mask2D" node (and/or a "mask_parent" property for Sprite2D)
Requirement: The software shall provide a Mask2D node to enable 2D node masking functionality, and/or add a mask_parent property to Sprite2D to allow sprites to be masked by parent nodes.

Issue Title: Add support for multiple displays/screens/monitors in Godot editor
Requirement: The Godot Editor must be enhanced to support multiple displays, allowing users to spread different panels or windows across several monitors for a more flexible, efficient workflow.

Issue Title: Add union types to Typed GDScript
Requirement: The system MUST support union types in Typed GDScript, enabling variables and function arguments to be declared with a union of multiple permitted types to improve type safety and flexibility.

Issue Title: Add "refactor" tooling to rename symbols in the script editor
Requirement: The script editor shall include a refactoring tool that enables users to safely rename symbols, ensuring that all instances of a symbol are updated consistently across the project with proper scope analysis.

Issue Title: Add public/private access modifiers to GDScript and autocompletion improvements
Requirement: The software shall support the declaration of public and private access modifiers within GDScript, and the autocompletion feature must be enhanced to recognize and suggest these modifiers in accordance with their visibility scopes.

Issue Title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons
Requirement: The system MUST support global plugins/universal addons that are installed once and then available across multiple projects. This requires an extension to the current project-based addon system to allow for centralized management of these plugins, including installation, update, and removal processes, while ensuring consistent behavior and compatibility across different project environments.

Issue Title: Implement a Rendering Compositor
Requirement: The system shall implement a rendering compositor that enables flexible, real-time composition of rendered image layers. The compositor must support multiple input sources, customizable blending modes, and configurable processing passes while providing an intuitive interface for developers to define, modify, and manage compositing workflows.

Issue Title: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node (inspired by the new 2D TileMap)
Requirement: The system shall replace the existing GridMap node with an enhanced 3D TileMap node that leverages modern design principles and functionality inspired by the latest 2D TileMap, providing improved usability, performance, and feature parity between 2D and 3D tile-based workflows.

Issue Title: Add array unpacking/destructuring to GDScript
Requirement: GDScript shall implement array unpacking/destructuring syntax to allow for more concise assignment of array elements to multiple variables in a single expression.

Issue Title: Calinou doesn't sleep
Requirement: The system shall include a configurable mechanism that prevents any automatic sleep or idle state activation for a designated user session (referred to as “Calinou”), ensuring that when the override is enabled, the application remains fully active regardless of inactivity or power-saving triggers.

Issue Title: Add proper and complete support for multi-pass shaders
Requirement: The system shall provide full and complete support for multi-pass shaders, enabling developers to create and utilize shaders that consist of multiple rendering passes. This includes a clear and documented API for defining, managing, and executing shader passes, ensuring compatibility across platforms and proper integration with rendering pipelines.

Issue Title: Godot C# GDExtension Roadmap Discussion
Requirement: The system shall provide a documented roadmap for integrating and evolving C# support using the GDExtension framework. This roadmap must clearly outline development milestones, integration strategies, compatibility considerations with current APIs, and planned updates, ensuring a transparent evolution of C# support within the engine.

Issue Title: Add literal quoted strings with embedded variables (f-strings) to GDScript
Requirement: GDScript shall support literal quoted strings with embedded variables—inspired by f-string functionality—allowing developers to interpolate variable values directly within string literals using a designated, intuitive syntax without additional concatenation, thereby simplifying and clarifying string formatting in the language.

Issue Title: Implement Terrain
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a dedicated terrain system within the engine that supports efficient creation, modification, and rendering of terrains. The system should include customizable terrain features (e.g., sculpting and texturing), support for multiple terrain types, and tools for level-of-detail management to ensure performance and scalability.

Issue Title: Improve the performance of the GDScript VM
Requirement: The GDScript Virtual Machine must be optimized to improve execution performance, reducing runtime overhead and increasing efficiency during common operations without sacrificing compatibility with existing scripts.

Issue Title: Add procedural and parametrizable audio support
Requirement: The software shall include a module for procedural and parameterizable audio generation, enabling users to dynamically generate and customize audio elements based on adjustable parameters and algorithms.

Issue Title: Rework the Tilemap terrain system to improve its usability
Requirement: The Tilemap terrain system shall be redesigned and refactored to improve its ease-of-use, enabling developers to intuitively create, edit, and manage terrain with enhanced flexibility and efficiency.

Issue Title: Implement namespaces in GDScript
Requirement: Implement a namespace system in GDScript that allows developers to organize classes and symbols into distinct, reusable logical groupings. This feature should enable the declaration and usage of namespaces to prevent naming conflicts, support aliasing, and integrate seamlessly with the existing GDScript syntax and module system.

Issue Title: Add WebGPU support
Requirement: The software shall integrate WebGPU as a rendering backend, enabling the engine to utilize modern GPU hardware features and APIs for improved performance and enhanced graphics capabilities across supported platforms.

Issue Title: Obfuscate GDScript in production export
Requirement: The software must provide a configurable obfuscation option for GDScript during production export, ensuring that the exported code remains functional while being difficult to reverse-engineer.

Issue Title: Implement a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array
Requirement: The system shall implement a new Set primitive type to complement the existing Dictionary and Array types. This Set type must efficiently store unique values, support standard set operations (such as union, intersection, and difference), and integrate seamlessly with Godot's scripting languages and core data structures.

Issue Title: Implement a code formatter for GDScript in the script editor
Requirement: The system shall include an integrated GDScript code formatter within the script editor to automatically format code according to standardized style guidelines, enhancing readability and consistency.

Issue Title: Implement method overloading in GDScript
Requirement: The software shall support method overloading in GDScript, enabling developers to define multiple methods with the same name but different parameter types or counts.

Issue Title: Add support for variadic functions (varargs) to GDScript
Requirement: The GDScript language shall support variadic functions, allowing developers to define functions with a variable number of arguments (varargs) that can be accessed and processed within the function body.

Issue Title: rustdoc support for per-parameter documentation
Requirement: The rustdoc tool MUST be enhanced to allow documentation to be added and rendered for each individual parameter of functions, enabling authors to provide detailed descriptions for each argument in a clear and structured manner.

Issue Title: Linking with LLD
Requirement: The Rust compiler must be enhanced to support linking via LLD. Users should be able to select LLD as the linker through command-line flags or configuration options, ensuring full compatibility with existing Rust targets and build workflows.

Issue Title: A new compiler flag: "link everything statically or die, dammit!"
Requirement: Add a new compiler flag that enforces static linking for all dependencies. When this flag is enabled, the compiler must verify that every library and dependency is linked statically if any component requires dynamic linking, the compilation should fail with an appropriate error message.

Issue Title: Need negative trait bound
Requirement: The Rust compiler shall be enhanced to support negative trait bounds, enabling users to specify constraints indicating that a type must not implement a particular trait.

Issue Title: Crate local state for procedural macros?
Requirement: The language implementation MUST support crate-local persistent state for procedural macros, allowing macros within the same crate to store, update, and retrieve shared state across invocations while ensuring that such state remains isolated from other crates.

Issue Title: Include images in rustdoc output
Requirement: The documentation generator (rustdoc) shall be enhanced to support embedding images within generated documentation. This functionality must allow image inclusion via markdown or designated directives, ensuring they render correctly in the final output across all supported platforms.

Issue Title: Using std::io::{Read, Write, Cursor} in a nostd environment
Requirement: The software shall provide support for using the functionalities equivalent to std::io::{Read, Write, Cursor} in a no_std environment, enabling developers to utilize similar I/O abstractions without relying on the full standard library.

Issue Title: Provide a means of turning iterators into fixed-size arrays
Requirement: The software shall provide a standardized API that allows conversion of iterators into fixed-size arrays. This functionality must ensure that the conversion is performed safely with compile-time guarantees or runtime error handling if the iterator does not yield exactly the required number of elements.

Issue Title: Add function to make paths absolute, which is different from canonicalization
Requirement: The software shall provide a new function that converts a given path to its absolute form without performing canonicalization, meaning it should not resolve symbolic links or verify the file system's actual structure.

Issue Title: Proc macros: ability to refer to a specific crate/symbol (something similar to `$crate`)
Requirement: The system MUST allow procedural macros to explicitly reference a specific crate or symbol, analogous to the `$crate` mechanism available for declarative macros, ensuring deterministic resolution of symbols even when crates are renamed or re-imported.

Issue Title: Inclusive version of take_while
Requirement: Provide an iterator adapter method, tentatively named inclusive_take_while, that iterates over elements until and including the first element for which the predicate returns false, then terminates. The implementation must integrate seamlessly with Rust's standard iterator traits and maintain performance characteristics comparable to take_while.

Issue Title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
Requirement: Requirement: The language must allow initialization of an array of Option<T> using the [None n] syntax without requiring that T implements the std::marker::Copy trait.

Issue Title: Add ability to ignore tests at runtime.
Requirement: The software shall provide a mechanism to mark tests for runtime exclusion, allowing designated tests to be skipped during execution unless explicitly enabled. This feature must integrate with existing testing frameworks and support both annotation-based and command-line options to control test execution.

Issue Title: Add Vec::contains_ref which is worse for inference but less restrictive than Vec::contains
Requirement: Implement a new method, Vec::contains_ref, that checks whether a vector contains an element by accepting a reference to the element. This method must use less restrictive trait bounds than Vec::contains, even if this results in less optimal inference performance, while still correctly determining element presence based on equality.

Issue Title: Feature request: Use 'trampolines' to make most of the body of a generic function non-generic
Requirement: The compiler shall implement support for trampolines in generic functions such that the majority of the function body is compiled as non-generic code, reducing monomorphization overhead and improving compile-time performance without altering the observable behavior of generic functions.

Issue Title: Subslice search
Requirement: The system shall provide an API function that locates the first occurrence of a specified subslice within a given slice, returning the starting index if found or an appropriate index value (e.g., None) if not. This functionality must support generic slice types and be optimized for performance using efficient search algorithms.

Issue Title: Use mold as default linker?
Requirement: The Rust compiler's build system shall be updated to use mold as the default linker on all supported platforms, automatically falling back to the current linker when mold is not available or compatible, in order to improve linking performance while preserving existing functionality.

Issue Title: rustdoc: `--enable-index-page` integration with cargo?
Requirement: Requirement: Integrate rustdoc's --enable-index-page feature with Cargo so that when Cargo is used to build and document Rust projects, an index page is automatically generated and properly linked to the project documentation. The implementation should ensure that users can opt in to this behavior via Cargo configuration or command-line options, and that the resulting documentation site includes a functional, navigable index page.

Issue Title: lint against unexpectedly late drop for temporaries in match scrutinee expressions
Requirement: The system MUST include a lint that detects and warns when temporaries created within match scrutinee expressions have been dropped later than expected, ensuring developers are alerted to potential unintended side effects from unexpectedly delayed drop semantics.

Issue Title: Support Windows kernel mode for driver development
Requirement: The system shall support Windows kernel mode by providing the necessary language features, tools, and libraries to enable the development, compilation, and debugging of Windows kernel drivers.

Issue Title: Struct initializer `..x` syntax should work for other structs with structurally equal subset of fields
Requirement: The compiler must be enhanced to allow a struct initializer using the .. syntax with any struct that contains a structurally equal subset of fields. This feature should enable reusing field values between different struct types when their overlapping fields have identical names and types.

Issue Title: [libs] Add `TcpStream::keepalive` and `TcpStream::set_keepalive`
Requirement: The software shall add two new functions to TcpStream: keepalive and set_keepalive. These functions must allow users to retrieve and configure the TCP keepalive settings, respectively, and should work reliably on all supported platforms by appropriately handling platform-specific variations in TCP keepalive behavior.

Issue Title: format_args! is slow
Requirement: The implementation of format_args! must be optimized to reduce its runtime overhead, ensuring that formatted string operations perform faster without sacrificing functionality or backward compatibility.

Issue Title: Add support for splitting linker invocation to a second execution of `rustc`
Requirement: The rustc compiler shall be enhanced to support splitting the linker invocation into a separate execution of rustc. This feature must allow the compilation process to offload the linking step to a second rustc invocation without affecting the correctness or performance of the overall compilation, while maintaining backward compatibility with existing build workflows.

Issue Title: Scan is overly specialized
Requirement: The system shall generalize the implementation of the iterator scan function to remove overly specialized constraints, allowing it to accept a broader range of closure types and use cases while maintaining backward compatibility.

Issue Title: RFC: Introduce `setup`, `teardown`, and `fixture` attributes for `cargo test`
Requirement: The system shall support new attributes—namely, "setup", "teardown", and "fixture"—for functions used in tests, allowing users to define, register, and execute test fixtures, initialization routines, and cleanup procedures automatically during the "cargo test" process.

Issue Title: Make `pub` in a binary equivalent to `pub(crate)` for diagnostics
Requirement: Binary crate items declared with the pub visibility modifier SHOULD be treated equivalently to pub(crate) for diagnostic purposes, ensuring that the diagnostics reflect that the item is only accessible within the current crate unless explicitly re-exported.

Issue Title: Feature Requst: Add regex support to test filters
Requirement: The system shall support filtering tests using regular expressions, allowing users to specify regex patterns to match test names when running tests. This functionality should integrate with the current test filtering mechanism, providing a clear command-line interface option and ensuring that regex patterns are safely and efficiently applied during test execution.

Issue Title: Add support for `#[doc(since="version")]` attribute

Issue Title: Provide UnixPath and WindowsPath (ditto PathBuf) on all platforms
Requirement: The system shall expose UnixPath and WindowsPath types (including their owning counterparts like UnixPathBuf and WindowsPathBuf) on all supported platforms, enabling applications to perform platform-specific path manipulations regardless of the underlying operating system.

Issue Title: plugin: add Windows support
Requirement: The plugin package MUST be enhanced to support Windows, enabling the loading and execution of plugins on this platform consistent with its behavior on other supported systems, and include appropriate documentation and tests.

Issue Title: net/http: support HTTP/3
Requirement: The software shall add support for HTTP/3 to the net/http package, enabling both client and server implementations to establish connections using the QUIC protocol. Issue Title: cmd/compile: implement powerpc 32-bit backend (ppc32)

Issue Title: x/pkgsite: generate static docs
Requirement: The system shall generate a complete set of static HTML documentation for Go packages, allowing users to host the documentation without requiring dynamic backend support.

Issue Title: database/sql: missing escape functions
Requirement: The database/sql package MUST provide a set of built-in escape functions that safely and consistently process user input for use in SQL queries, helping prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities and ensuring compatibility with various SQL dialects where applicable.

Issue Title: encoding/json: no way to preserve the order of map keys
Requirement: The encoding/json package shall be enhanced to allow preservation of map key order when encoding and decoding JSON objects. This feature must provide a way to retain the insertion order of keys in maps so that JSON output and input parsing respects the original key sequence.

Issue Title: x/tools/gopls: annotations for implementations of interfaces
Requirement: The tool shall display annotations that indicate, on interface declarations, the locations and details of all implementing types. These annotations must update dynamically as the code evolves, and support seamless navigation from an interface to its implementations.

Issue Title: runtime: implement WASM-GC
Requirement: The Go runtime shall implement WebAssembly garbage collection (WASM-GC) support, enabling efficient and compliant garbage collection for Go applications compiled to WebAssembly.

Issue Title: x/pkgsite: API for pkg.go.dev
Requirement: The system shall provide a public API for pkg.go.dev that allows clients to retrieve package metadata, documentation, versioning information, and search results programmatically, ensuring consistency and up-to-date synchronization with the pkgsite data.

Issue Title: cmd/go: 'go mod why' should have an answer for every module in 'go list -m all'
Requirement: The go mod why command must provide an explanation for every module listed by go list -m all, ensuring that each module's inclusion is clearly justified, even if the dependency is indirect.

Issue Title: cmd/go: allow verifying vendored code
Requirement: The go command shall include an option to verify the integrity of code in vendor directories by comparing vendored files against their corresponding module sources or checksums, ensuring that the vendored code has not been altered from its verified origin.

Issue Title: plugin: Add support for closing plugins
Requirement: The Go plugin package MUST include a mechanism for closing plugins after they are loaded to ensure proper cleanup and resource deallocation. This functionality should provide a well-defined interface for gracefully shutting down a plugin and releasing any associated resources, preventing resource leaks and ensuring robust plugin lifecycle management.

Issue Title: reflect: NamedOf
Requirement: The reflect package MUST include a new function NamedOf that, given a value or type, returns its declared (named) identifier. For named types, NamedOf should return the documented name, and for types without an explicit name (e.g., anonymous types), it MUST return an empty string. The implementation MUST integrate seamlessly with existing reflect functionality and adhere to established conventions regarding type metadata.

Issue Title: proposal: database/sql: support a way to perform bulk actions
Requirement: The database/sql package MUST include a new bulk actions API that enables developers to perform multiple SQL operations efficiently in a single call. This API should support executing a set of queries or prepared statements in a batch, optionally within a transaction, to optimize performance and reduce round-trip latency. The implementation must ensure compatibility with existing driver abstractions and gracefully handle driver-specific limitations, while providing clear error reporting for failures in any individual statement within the batch operation.

Issue Title: x/tools/gopls: support change signature refactoring
Requirement: The tool shall support a "change signature" refactoring operation that allows users to modify the parameters and return types of functions and methods. Issue Title: cmd/link: support msvc object files
Requirement: The Go linker (cmd/link) SHALL be enhanced to support the MSVC object file format, enabling users to link MSVC-compiled object files into Go binaries.

Issue Title: cmd/fix: automate migrations for simple deprecations
Requirement: The system shall enhance the cmd/fix tool to automatically identify and migrate simple deprecations in Go code, ensuring that deprecated constructs are replaced with their updated equivalents during codebase maintenance.

Issue Title: x/vuln: add support for suppressing vulnerabilities by ID
Requirement: The vulnerability module must include support to suppress vulnerabilities by their ID, allowing users to designate specific vulnerability identifiers to be excluded from reports or analyses.

Issue Title: compress/bzip2: implement bz2 encoder
Requirement: Implement a bz2 encoder in the compress/bzip2 package that encodes data using the bzip2 algorithm per its official specification. The implementation must provide a clear, well-documented API, support flexible encoding options, and include a comprehensive test suite to verify correctness and performance comparable to existing decompression functionality.

Issue Title: cmd/compile: coverage instrumentation for fuzzing
Requirement: The Go compiler shall include an option to enable fine-grained code coverage instrumentation during fuzz test builds. When activated, the compiler must generate and embed metadata that records execution paths, allowing fuzzing tools to accurately track which code regions have been exercised. This instrumentation should be configurable via command-line flags, incur minimal overhead in non-fuzzing builds, and integrate seamlessly with the existing fuzzing infrastructure to enhance automated test case generation and analysis.

Issue Title: cmd/go: add 'go get' options to update direct and indirect dependencies separately

Issue Title: cmd/go: subcommand as git merge tool for go.mod merge conflicts
Requirement: Implement a new subcommand within cmd/go that serves as a dedicated git merge tool for go.mod files. Issue Title: testing: exclude statically unreachable code in test coverage
Requirement: The test coverage tool must be updated to automatically detect and exclude statically unreachable code from its coverage calculations, ensuring that only code paths that can logically be executed are considered in test coverage metrics.

Issue Title: x/crypto: add BLAKE3 support
Requirement: Implement BLAKE3 support in the x/crypto package by adding a complete, standards-compliant implementation of the BLAKE3 hash algorithm—including its basic, keyed, and extendable output modes—with comprehensive tests and documentation to ensure secure and correct functionality.

Issue Title: crypto/tls: add PSK support
Requirement: The crypto/tls package MUST include support for Pre-Shared Key (PSK) cipher suites. All necessary functions, data structures, and configuration options required to integrate PSK cipher suites into the package MUST be designed and implemented in compliance with relevant security standards.

Issue Title: cmd/go: allow serving module under the subdirectory of git repository
Requirement: The Go command must be enhanced to support serving a Go module located in a subdirectory of a Git repository. Issue Title: cmd/compile: thread support for webassembly
Requirement: The Go compiler must provide support for multithreading on WebAssembly targets to enable concurrent execution in WebAssembly applications, including proper synchronization primitives and adherence to WebAssembly threading standards.

Issue Title: x/net/http2: support consuming PUSH_PROMISE streams in the client
Requirement: The HTTP/2 client implementation in the x/net/http2 package MUST be enhanced to properly consume and process PUSH_PROMISE streams as defined by the HTTP/2 specification.

Issue Title: x/tools/gopls: support for bazel-based projects
Requirement: The gopls tool shall provide built-in support for Bazel-based Go projects, including proper handling of Bazel build configurations, dependency resolution, and project structure so that users can seamlessly develop and navigate their Bazel-managed codebases using gopls features.

Issue Title: encoding/xml: add support for xml version 1.1
Requirement: The XML encoding library MUST be extended to support XML version 1.1. This feature should include appropriate parsing, encoding, and validation of XML 1.1 documents, while maintaining full compatibility with existing XML 1.0 functionality. All changes must be covered by unit tests and integrated into the current library's API in a backward compatible manner.

Issue Title: General MPS op coverage tracking issue

Requirement: The system shall add support for public/private access modifiers to GDScript and enhance autocompletion capabilities.

Requirement: The system shall provide comprehensive support for multi-pass shaders, allowing users to define, configure, and manage multiple shader passes for advanced rendering techniques.

Issue Title: x/tools/gopls: annotations for implementations of interfaces
Requirement: The system shall annotate implementations of interfaces in gopls, enabling users to easily identify and navigate to the definitions of interface implementations.

Issue Title: runtime: implement WASM-GC
Requirement: The runtime shall implement WebAssembly garbage collection (WASM-GC) to effectively manage memory in WebAssembly applications.

Issue Title: x/pkgsite: API for pkg.go.dev
Requirement: The system shall implement a public API for pkg.go.dev that exposes package documentation, metadata, and related information through secure, versioned endpoints.

Issue Title: cmd/go: 'go mod why' should have an answer for every module in 'go list -m all'
Requirement: The go command shall be updated so that the 'go mod why' command provides an explanatory response for every module listed by 'go list -m all'.

Issue Title: cmd/go: allow verifying vendored code
Requirement: The system shall support verifying the integrity of vendored code using the same verification mechanisms implemented for non-vendored code.

Issue Title: plugin: Add support for closing plugins
Requirement: The system shall add support for closing plugins to allow safe unloading and management of plugin resources.

Issue Title: reflect: NamedOf
Requirement: The reflect package shall provide a NamedOf function that returns the name of a given type.

Issue Title: proposal: database/sql: support a way to perform bulk actions
Requirement: The system shall extend the database/sql package to support bulk actions, enabling efficient execution of multiple database operations in a single transaction or request.

Issue Title: x/tools/gopls: support change signature refactoring
Requirement: The system shall implement change signature refactoring in x/tools/gopls, allowing users to modify function signatures and automatically propagate the changes across all call sites.

Issue Title: cmd/link: support msvc object files
Requirement: The system shall support linking of Microsoft Visual Studio (MSVC) object files within the cmd/link tool.

Issue Title: cmd/fix: automate migrations for simple deprecations
Requirement: The system shall automate migrations for simple deprecations in the cmd/fix tool.

Issue Title: x/vuln: add support for suppressing vulnerabilities by ID
Requirement: The system shall support suppressing vulnerabilities by their ID in the x/vuln package.

Issue Title: compress/bzip2: implement bz2 encoder
Requirement: The system shall implement a bz2 encoder in the compress/bzip2 package to support bz2 file encoding.

Issue Title: cmd/compile: coverage instrumentation for fuzzing
Requirement: The cmd/compile component shall incorporate coverage instrumentation to support fuzzing, capturing execution data to enhance fuzz test efficacy.

Issue Title: cmd/go: add 'go get' options to update direct and indirect dependencies separately
Requirement: The system shall extend the 'go get' command to include options for updating direct and indirect dependencies separately.

Issue Title: cmd/go: subcommand as git merge tool for go.mod merge conflicts
Requirement: The go command shall provide a subcommand that functions as a git merge tool specifically for merging go.mod files and resolving merge conflicts.

Issue Title: testing: exclude statically unreachable code in test coverage
Requirement: The testing framework shall exclude statically unreachable code from test coverage analysis to ensure accurate testing metrics.

Issue Title: x/crypto: add BLAKE3 support
Requirement: The x/crypto package shall provide full support for the BLAKE3 hash function, including its integration, implementation, and relevant documentation.

Issue Title: crypto/tls: add PSK support
Requirement: The crypto/tls package shall support pre-shared keys (PSKs) for establishing secure connections.

Issue Title: cmd/go: allow serving module under the subdirectory of git repository
Requirement: The system shall support serving a Go module from a subdirectory within a git repository.

Issue Title: cmd/compile: thread support for webassembly
Requirement: The compiler shall support multi-threading for WebAssembly targets to enable concurrent execution in Go programs.

Issue Title: x/net/http2: support consuming PUSH_PROMISE streams in the client
Requirement: The system shall enable the HTTP/2 client to support consuming PUSH_PROMISE streams.

Issue Title: x/tools/gopls: support for bazel-based projects
Requirement: The system shall support bazel-based projects in x/tools/gopls for improved compatibility with non-standard Go project structures.

Issue Title: encoding/xml: add support for xml version 1.1
Requirement: The system shall add support for XML version 1.1 to the encoding/xml package.

Issue Title: General MPS op coverage tracking issue
Requirement: Requirement: Develop and integrate a comprehensive tracking system for MPS (Metal Performance Shaders) operation coverage within PyTorch. The system must automatically identify, report, and monitor the level of support for each MPS operation in comparison to other backends. It should provide detailed metrics on missing or partially supported operations, enable filtering by op type and status, and offer actionable insights to guide future development efforts for expanding MPS compatibility.

Issue Title: ARM Mac 16-core Neural Engine
Requirement: Requirement: Implement native support for the ARM Mac 16-core Neural Engine in PyTorch. This support should provide accelerated computation on ARM-based Macs by leveraging the 16-core Neural Engine for tensor operations, neural network inference, and training tasks where applicable. The implementation must include API extensions, optimizations for kernel operations compatible with the Neural Engine, and fallbacks for unsupported operations, while ensuring compatibility with existing PyTorch workflows and deployment pipelines on ARM Mac systems.

Issue Title: PyPy support
Requirement: Requirement: Ensure full PyPy support within the PyTorch codebase and build system. The implementation shall include: • Verifying and updating the codebase to be compatible with the latest stable PyPy interpreter version. • Modifying build and packaging processes to correctly build and distribute PyTorch for PyPy environments. • Adapting and/or extending existing tests to account for PyPy-specific runtime behaviors and ensuring that the test suite passes reliably on PyPy. • Updating documentation to include instructions and known limitations for PyPy users. • Monitoring performance and identifying any potential optimizations or regressions when running on PyPy.

Issue Title: Implement similar PyTorch function as model.summary() in keras?
Requirement: Requirement: Introduce a built-in utility function in PyTorch (e.g., torch.summary) that provides a detailed, formatted overview of a model's architecture similarly to Keras's model.summary(). This utility should accept an instance of a neural network model and input shape(s) as arguments, and then output a summary including layer names, output shapes, parameter counts (trainable and non-trainable), and total parameters. The function should handle both sequential and complex dynamic models, support various model types (including nested modules), and be easily extensible to report additional metrics in future updates.

Issue Title: CPU version of PyTorch on PyPI
Requirement: Requirement: Provide a pre-built, CPU-only version of PyTorch available on PyPI, allowing users without GPU support to easily install and run PyTorch without requiring a full CUDA-enabled installation. The package should minimize dependencies related to GPU acceleration and be maintained in parallel with the main PyTorch distribution, with clear versioning and compatibility documentation.

Issue Title: Implement `numpy.random.choice` equivalent
Requirement: Requirement Title: Implement torch.random.choice Functionality Requirement Statement:  Introduce a new function, torch.random.choice, that replicates the behavior of numpy.random.choice. The function should accept both a 1-dimensional tensor (or integer representing a range of values) as the source from which to choose, and the following parameters:  1. size – to specify the number of elements to sample. 2. replace – a boolean indicating whether sampling is with replacement (default: True) or without replacement. 3. p – an optional probability tensor to specify the sampling likelihood of each element. The function must validate inputs, handle edge cases (e.g., non-replacement sampling when the size exceeds available unique elements), and perform efficiently on both CPU and GPU. The API should follow PyTorch coding conventions and support gradient propagation where applicable.

Issue Title: [RFC] Add tar-based IterableDataset implementation to PyTorch
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a tar-based IterableDataset for PyTorch that allows users to efficiently stream and iterate over data stored within tar archives. The implementation must: • Read data directly from tar files without requiring extraction to disk. • Support iterating over individual archive members as dataset samples. • Integrate seamlessly with PyTorch’s data loading API and support standard IterableDataset operations (e.g., sharding for distributed processing, parallel data loading, etc.). • Provide configurable options for handling file compression and reading performance optimizations. • Include robust error handling for corrupt archives and graceful fallback to default behavior. The feature should be well-documented, include unit tests and integration tests, and maintain compatibility with existing PyTorch data pipelines.

Issue Title: [Feature request] Let DistributedSampler take a Sampler as input
Requirement: Requirement ID: DS-001   Title: Allow DistributedSampler to Accept a Custom Sampler as Input   Description:   The DistributedSampler component in the library shall be enhanced to accept an instance of a Sampler as an input parameter. This custom sampler input will enable users to leverage specialized sampling strategies while maintaining distributed training capabilities.   Acceptance Criteria:   1. The DistributedSampler constructor shall include an optional parameter for a custom sampler, which will default to None if not provided.   2. When a custom sampler is provided, DistributedSampler shall utilize it for sampling data indices instead of its default deterministic sampling strategy.   3. The integration of a custom sampler must preserve the behavior of DistributedSampler in the context of data partitioning and shuffling for distributed environments.   4. Unit tests shall be implemented to verify that DistributedSampler correctly uses the provided custom sampler and falls back to default behavior when no custom sampler is supplied.   5. Documentation shall be updated to explain the new parameter, its use cases, and provide sample code demonstrating its application.

Issue Title: [FYI] NestedTensor Project Progress
Requirement: Requirement: Integrate a NestedTensor feature into PyTorch that supports the creation and manipulation of collections of tensors with varying shapes without requiring explicit padding. The implementation must provide a clear and consistent API for constructing NestedTensors, enable common tensor operations (such as arithmetic, indexing, slicing, and reduction) directly on NestedTensor objects, and integrate seamlessly with PyTorch’s autograd mechanism for automatic differentiation. Comprehensive documentation and tests must accompany the release to ensure robust integration and ease of use.

Issue Title: [Proposal] Data reading framework for PyTorch (Hive, MySQL, S3 etc.)
Requirement: Requirement: Develop a flexible and extensible data reading framework for PyTorch that can interface with various data sources—including Hive, MySQL, S3, and other similar systems. The framework must offer a unified API to connect, query, and retrieve data, with built-in support for configurable connection parameters, error handling, data caching, and scalability. It should seamlessly integrate with PyTorch’s existing data pipeline and dataset abstractions, ensuring efficient data access and preprocessing for training workflows.

Issue Title: Statically checked tensor shapes
Requirement: Requirement ID: PT-PY-001 Title: Statically Checked Tensor Shapes Description: Extend PyTorch's tensor API to allow developers to perform static checks on tensor shapes at compile time. The implementation must support compile-time verification of tensor shape compatibility for operations, ensuring that incompatible shapes are caught before execution. The solution should integrate with existing type-checking tools and workflows, allowing for explicit shape annotations and providing clear error messages when shape mismatches occur. The feature must be backward compatible with existing PyTorch code and configurable to enable or disable static shape checking as needed. Acceptance Criteria: 1. Developers can annotate tensor functions with expected shape information. 2. The system performs compile-time checks to verify that tensor operations are used with compatible shapes. 3. Informative error messages are provided when a shape mismatch is detected during compilation. 4. Integration with common type-checking tools (e.g., mypy, Pyright) is ensured. 5. Backward compatibility: Existing PyTorch code should continue to function correctly without requiring annotations. 6. Documentation and examples are provided to demonstrate usage and integration into existing workflows. Constraints: The implementation must not introduce significant runtime overhead and must maintain or improve overall codebase maintainability.

Issue Title: [RFC] DataLoader architecture updates and TarDataset implementation
Requirement: Requirement: Update the PyTorch DataLoader architecture to support an extensible dataset interface that includes a new TarDataset implementation. The TarDataset shall allow users to load data directly from tar archive files without requiring manual extraction. It must support efficient, streaming access to individual file entries within the archive, provide customizable options for file filtering and transformations, and be compatible with existing DataLoader features such as multi-threaded/multi-process data loading, batching, and shuffling. The implementation must maintain backward compatibility with the current DataLoader API, be thoroughly unit and integration tested, and include complete documentation and usage examples.

Issue Title: Transformer Lack of Embedding Layer and Positional Encodings
Requirement: Requirement: Extend the Transformer module to include a dedicated embedding layer and support for positional encodings. The new component should accept tokenized input sequences and generate appropriate embeddings by mapping input tokens to continuous vector representations, then add or combine positional encodings to capture sequence order information. The implementation must be flexible, allowing users to choose between fixed (e.g., sinusoidal) or learnable positional encoding mechanisms and support different embedding dimensions as configured by the user. This enhancement must integrate seamlessly with existing transformer workflows and maintain compatibility with current PyTorch transformer modules and API conventions.

Issue Title: [RFC] TorchStore - A Shared-Memory Tensor Store
Requirement: Title: TorchStore – A Shared-Memory Tensor Store Requirement: Implement a shared-memory tensor store ("TorchStore") integrated into PyTorch that enables multiple processes to allocate, access, modify, and deallocate tensors within a common shared memory region. The system should provide API endpoints for creating a tensor store, inserting tensors, retrieving tensors by identifiers, updating stored tensors, and deleting tensors. It must include robust concurrency control mechanisms (e.g., locking or atomic operations) to ensure data consistency and thread-safety during simultaneous accesses. The solution should be optimized for high-performance interprocess communication, facilitate efficient memory management, and seamlessly integrate with PyTorch’s existing tensor operations and distributed training workflows. Detailed documentation and usage examples must be provided to support external developers in leveraging TorchStore for multi-GPU, multi-process, and distributed computing scenarios.

Issue Title: [FR][RFC] Build a serving framework to host and serve trained PyTorch models
Requirement: Requirement Statement: Develop an integrated PyTorch model serving framework that allows users to host and serve trained PyTorch models in production environments. The framework must provide simple deployment mechanisms, support for standard serving protocols (e.g., REST and gRPC), and features such as batch processing, scalability (including auto-scaling), robust monitoring/logging, and fault tolerance. It should seamlessly integrate with the existing PyTorch ecosystem, allow for custom extensions, and include comprehensive documentation and examples to aid adoption and ensure ease of use by both developers and researchers.

Issue Title: [RFC] DeepSpeed + PT Distributed Integration
Requirement: Requirement Statement: Integrate DeepSpeed’s distributed training optimizations with PyTorch’s native distributed framework to provide a seamless, high-performance distributed training experience. The solution must: • Enable users to harness DeepSpeed’s advanced memory management, zero redundancy optimizer (ZeRO), and other performance improvements directly within PyTorch’s distributed training workflows. • Provide configurable interfaces and APIs that allow users to opt in to DeepSpeed enhancements with minimal changes to existing PyTorch code. • Ensure compatibility across various distributed setups, including multi-node and multi-GPU configurations, while maintaining consistency in error handling, logging, and debugging across both DeepSpeed and PyTorch distributed modules. • Include comprehensive documentation and sample code that clearly demonstrates the integration process, configuration options, and best practices. • Implement extensive testing (unit, integration, and performance tests) to validate that the combined system meets performance, scalability, and correctness requirements.

Issue Title: Parallel Associative Scan
Requirement: Requirement Statement: Implement a parallel associative scan operation within PyTorch that computes prefix sums using the associative property. The operation must support tensors on both CPU and GPU, integrate seamlessly with PyTorch’s tensor operations and automatic differentiation, and be optimized to effectively leverage multi-core and parallel processing architectures. The implementation should include comprehensive unit tests and benchmarks to validate correctness, performance, and compatibility with existing PyTorch semantics.

Issue Title: Support for `uint16`, `uint32`, and `uint64`
Requirement: The system shall add support for unsigned integer data types uint16, uint32, and uint64 throughout the PyTorch framework, including tensor creation, manipulation, storage, and operations that interact with these types, while ensuring consistent behavior with existing integer data types and maintaining backward compatibility.

Issue Title: Feature request: INT4 format support
Requirement: Requirement Statement: Add comprehensive native support for the INT4 tensor data format in PyTorch. The implementation must enable users to create, manipulate, and perform arithmetic operations on INT4 tensors. This support should include conversion utilities between INT4 and existing tensor formats, optimized computational kernels (with hardware acceleration where available), and integration with existing modules and libraries. All API modifications must be fully documented to ensure clarity for users, and backward compatibility with current PyTorch functionalities must be maintained.

Issue Title: [feature request] Simple and Efficient way to get gradients of each element of a sum
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a feature in PyTorch's autograd engine that allows users to easily and efficiently retrieve the gradient for each individual element when computing the sum of tensor elements. This functionality should work seamlessly with existing autograd operations, support batch processing to maintain performance, and provide API interfaces that integrate with current PyTorch tensor and module frameworks. The implementation must ensure minimal overhead compared to current gradient computations and include comprehensive documentation and tests to validate correctness and performance across typical use cases.

Issue Title: non-negative least squares solver feature request
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a non-negative least squares (NNLS) solver in PyTorch that provides an API function accepting a coefficient matrix A and a right-hand side vector b (or batched versions thereof) as torch Tensors. The function should compute a solution vector x that minimizes the squared error ||Ax - b||² subject to x ≥ 0. It must support gradient propagation where applicable, allow optional tolerance and iteration limit parameters to control the convergence behavior, and be efficiently scalable to moderate-to-large problem sizes. Comprehensive unit tests and documentation (usage examples, input requirements, and limitations) must accompany the implementation.

Issue Title: [RFC] RPC Based Distributed Model Parallel
Requirement: Implement RPC-based Distributed Model Parallel functionality in PyTorch. The feature must enable distributed training by leveraging Remote Procedure Calls (RPC) to split model computation across multiple nodes, allowing for efficient communication and synchronization. It should support flexible configurations to partition models across worker nodes, provide clear APIs for launching RPC processes, allow dynamic scaling, and integrate fault-tolerance mechanisms. Comprehensive documentation, sample scripts, and performance benchmarks are required to guide users in deploying and optimizing distributed training scenarios using this new paradigm.

Issue Title: [Poll] Support DistributedDataParallel (DDP) in PyTorch C++ API (libtorch)
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance libtorch to support DistributedDataParallel (DDP) functionality. The implementation must enable model replication across processes, automatic gradient synchronization, and integrated process group management, providing feature parity with Python’s DDP API. The solution should expose a C++ API allowing users to easily initialize DDP for multi-process training, configure communication backends, and manage fault tolerance mechanisms, accompanied by comprehensive documentation and example usage.

Issue Title: DataLoader with option to re-use worker processes
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a configurable worker process re-use option in the DataLoader. When enabled, the DataLoader should maintain a pool of persistent worker processes across multiple iterations (epochs) to reduce initialization overhead and improve data fetching performance. This feature must be controllable via a new parameter (e.g., persistent_workers) in the DataLoader API, and should support all standard DataLoader functionalities including multi-processing, dataset shuffling, and batch prefetching. Additionally, the implementation must ensure proper resource cleanup upon termination (e.g., graceful process shutdown during interruption) and maintain backward compatibility with existing DataLoader usage.

Issue Title: [RFC] PT2-Friendly Traceable, Functional Collective Communication APIs
Requirement: Requirement: Introduce a new set of traceable, functional collective communication APIs in PyTorch that are PT2-friendly. These APIs must provide functional semantics for common collective operations (e.g., broadcast, reduce, gather, scatter) with explicit, traceable execution steps that enable debugging, performance analysis, and integration with PyTorch’s execution tracing infrastructure. The design shall ensure that the APIs support stateless, deterministic behavior for both distributed training and inference scenarios, while being fully compatible with existing PyTorch tensor and distributed communication abstractions.

Issue Title: [feature request] Global GPU Flag
Requirement: Requirement: Introduce a global configuration flag (e.g., use_global_gpu) within PyTorch that, when enabled, forces all GPU-eligible operations to default to GPU execution. This flag should be accessible via a central configuration API, configurable at runtime, and able to override module-specific device settings unless explicitly overridden. The implementation must ensure consistency across all modules, support dynamic switching during application execution, and include appropriate error handling and fallback for systems without GPU support.

Issue Title: OpenCL 3.0 support: support every GPU on earth through rusticl
Requirement: Requirement: Add integrated support for OpenCL 3.0 in PyTorch to enable GPU acceleration on any OpenCL 3.0–compliant device. This support should leverage the Rust-based OpenCL implementation (rusticl) and provide a seamless interface for PyTorch operations, ensuring that the framework can execute computations on a broad range of GPUs across different vendors. The implementation must include robust testing and validation across multiple hardware platforms to guarantee compatibility and performance.

Issue Title: Zero-copy on shared memory of NVIDIA Jetson devices
Requirement: Requirement Statement: The PyTorch framework shall enable zero-copy operations on shared memory for NVIDIA Jetson devices. This functionality must allow direct data sharing between processes without additional memory copying, thereby reducing latency and improving performance. The implementation should utilize the available shared memory mechanisms on NVIDIA Jetson platforms and ensure compatibility with existing PyTorch tensor operations. Comprehensive testing and validation must be provided to confirm that the zero-copy functionality works reliably across typical usage scenarios on NVIDIA Jetson devices.

Issue Title: Feature Request: Easier to extend base RNN implementation
Requirement: The system MUST allow developers to extend the base RNN implementation with minimal effort by providing a simplified interface and extension points. This includes: • A clear API for subclassing that exposes core RNN functionalities and hidden states. • Well-documented callback hooks and extension methods for custom cell behavior and recurrent operations. • Sample code and comprehensive documentation that demonstrate how to integrate and override base methods. • Backward compatibility guarantees ensuring that existing models using the current base implementation continue to work correctly. All changes MUST be accompanied by unit tests and integration tests to verify that custom extensions function as expected.

Issue Title: Return attention weights in nn.Transformer
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance the nn.Transformer module by adding an option to return attention weights. This functionality should be configurable via a new parameter (e.g., return_attention_weights) in the module’s initialization, allowing users to enable or disable the retrieval of attention weights during the forward pass. When enabled, the forward method should output a tuple containing both the transformer’s standard output and the corresponding attention weights for analysis or debugging. The implementation should maintain backward compatibility with existing models and provide clear, documented examples and tests for the new functionality.

Issue Title: Code Push / Hot Update / out of band updates
Requirement: Requirement: Implement an out-of-band update mechanism in Flutter that enables secure, runtime code and asset updates (i.e., hot updates) without requiring users to download a new version from app stores. The solution must include: • A secure update service that verifies digital signatures and integrity of update packages before application. • Support for updating Dart code, assets, and other eligible resources at runtime while ensuring compatibility with existing app states. • A rollback mechanism to revert to the previous stable version in case of update failures. • Compliance with platform policies and integration guidelines to ensure that updates do not violate app store rules. • Detailed logging and error reporting for transparency and troubleshooting. This feature shall be designed with extensibility and safety as priorities, allowing developers to seamlessly deliver incremental updates post-deployment.
