Issue Title: Enable "hot reload" (not just "hot restart") for Flutter Web
Requirement: Requirement: Implement Hot Reload for Flutter Web The Flutter Web development experience shall be enhanced by adding a hot reload feature that updates the application state with code changes without performing a full restart. The hot reload mechanism must work similarly to the existing hot reload on mobile platforms, preserving the current app state and efficiently applying code modifications in real-time. This feature must include error handling, logging, and fallbacks to hot restart when necessary, and be thoroughly tested across supported web browsers.

Issue Title: Let flutter be installable via homebrew
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a Homebrew formula for Flutter, allowing users to install and update the Flutter SDK via Homebrew on macOS. This should include the packaging of the Flutter SDK, its dependencies, and any necessary post-install configuration steps to ensure full functionality consistent with Flutter’s current installation process. The implementation must follow Homebrew guidelines, provide proper versioning, and support future updates and maintenance.

Issue Title: Improve the indexability (SEO) of Flutter apps on the web
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance the SEO (Search Engine Optimization) capabilities of Flutter web applications by ensuring that rendered content, meta tags, and structured data are available and indexable by search engines. The implementation must include: 1. An approach to generate or support pre-rendered or server-side rendered content without sacrificing Flutter’s rich interactivity. 2. Customizable mechanisms to define meta tags (e.g., title, description, canonical tags) and structured data directly from Flutter code or configuration. 3. Comprehensive documentation and guidelines for developers to optimize their Flutter web apps for search engine indexing. 4. Compatibility checks to ensure that SEO improvements do not degrade overall application performance or user experience.

Issue Title: Support multiple windows for desktop shells
Requirement: Requirement Title: Multi-Window Support for Desktop Platforms Description: Implement functionality in the Flutter framework that enables applications to create and manage multiple top-level windows on desktop platforms (Windows, macOS, and Linux). This support should allow applications to open, close, and manage multiple independent windows concurrently, with each window capable of rendering its own Flutter UI. The implementation must integrate with the native windowing systems on each platform and provide a unified API for Flutter developers. Functional Requirements: 1. Provide an API that allows creation, display, and disposal of additional windows. 2. Ensure each window can run independent Flutter widget trees and support standard window management operations. 3. Include mechanisms to communicate between multiple windows if required by the application. 4. Integrate with the underlying operating system's window management for seamless user experience. 5. Maintain backward compatibility with existing single-window applications. Non-Functional Requirements: 1. Ensure performance efficiency in managing multiple windows, especially regarding resource utilization. 2. Guarantee a consistent developer API across supported desktop platforms. 3. Provide comprehensive documentation and examples for developers on using the multi-window API. Acceptance Criteria: 1. Demonstrate the creation and management of multiple simultaneous windows in a sample Flutter desktop application. 2. Validate that each window operates independently and can be individually closed without affecting others. 3. Confirm proper integration with native operating system window management features on Windows, macOS, and Linux. 4. Detailed documentation and migration guide are available for developers to adopt multi-window patterns in existing applications.

Issue Title: Implement PlatformView support on macOS
Requirement: Requirement: Implement support for PlatformViews on macOS to enable embedding and rendering of native views within Flutter applications. This implementation should provide a consistent API that integrates with the existing Flutter framework architecture, allowing developers to leverage platform-specific native components seamlessly on macOS. The solution must handle view synchronization, lifecycle management, and event propagation, ensuring compatibility with current Flutter rendering and tooling practices on macOS.

Issue Title: Server-side rendering for Flutter web
Requirement: Requirement: Implement server-side rendering capabilities for Flutter web applications to improve load performance and optimize content for SEO. This feature must enable generating initial HTML content on the server, support hydration on the client for interactive updates, and provide configuration options for developers to enable or disable server-side rendering. The implementation should integrate seamlessly with existing Flutter web compilation workflows and be compatible with standard Flutter web development practices.

Issue Title: Apple CarPlay / Android Auto support?
Requirement: Requirement: Implement cross-platform support within Flutter for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, enabling developers to build and deploy applications that can interface with in-car systems. The implementation must provide an abstraction layer to handle communication with the native operating systems' CarPlay and Auto frameworks, adhere to each platform's UI/UX guidelines, and expose APIs that allow developers to customize car-specific interactions and display elements. The solution should include documentation, sample projects, and guidelines for integration while ensuring compatibility with existing Flutter plugins and applications.

Issue Title: [google_maps_flutter] Support Widgets as markers
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance the google_maps_flutter plugin to allow developers to use Flutter widgets as custom markers on Google Maps. This feature should enable widgets to be rendered as markers, support their lifecycle management, and allow interactions such as taps. The implementation must ensure consistent rendering performance and proper updates of widget states in response to map movements or marker property changes. Backward compatibility must be maintained for existing implementations that use image-based markers.

Issue Title: Implement PlatformView support on Windows
Requirement: Requirement: Implement comprehensive PlatformView support on Windows within the Flutter framework. This feature must enable developers to embed and render native Windows views seamlessly inside a Flutter application. The implementation should include: • A robust integration between Flutter’s rendering engine and native Windows UI components, ensuring proper layout, scaling, and performance. • Handling of input events (mouse, keyboard, touch) in a manner that aligns with both Flutter’s gesture system and native Windows event propagation. • Support for hardware acceleration and compatibility with existing Flutter engine optimizations on Windows. • Proper initialization, lifecycle management, and cleanup of embedded Windows views. • Comprehensive documentation and sample code to assist developers in integrating native Windows views within their Flutter apps. • Thorough testing on various Windows versions to ensure stability, responsiveness, and correctness. This requirement will allow Flutter applications to leverage native Windows capabilities alongside Flutter-rendered UI components, delivering a unified and high-performance user experience.

Issue Title: Customizable project structure (platforms)
Requirement: Requirement: The system MUST allow users to customize the project structure for different platforms by providing configurable options to define and modify the organization of directories, files, and platform-specific configurations. This customization SHOULD enable developers to adjust, add, or remove default platform directories and to update build configurations accordingly, ensuring that the project structure aligns with non-standard and project-specific organizational patterns.

Issue Title: Add support for visionOS
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance Flutter to support visionOS by implementing platform-specific adaptations, APIs, and tooling necessary for developers to build, test, and deploy Flutter applications on visionOS devices.

Issue Title: [web] Support compute on separate thread in Flutter Web
Requirement: Requirement: Implement support for executing compute functions on a separate thread in Flutter Web.  The solution must allow developers to run compute-intensive operations in a dedicated worker (or isolate) without blocking the main UI thread to improve performance. This includes: • Extending the Flutter Web platform to recognize and execute compute calls in a non-blocking manner, potentially using browser web workers or equivalent mechanisms. • Providing an API that is consistent with compute functionality on other platforms. • Ensuring synchronization between the separate thread and the main UI context. • Including thorough error handling and recovery in case of worker failures. • Documenting usage patterns, limitations, and performance trade-offs for Flutter Web developers.

Issue Title: Support home and lock screen widgets
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance Flutter by adding native support for home screen and lock screen widgets. This functionality should allow developers to create, customize, and integrate widgets that display on both home and lock screens of supported devices, with appropriate APIs for managing widget data updates, user interactions, and lifecycle events in a consistent cross-platform manner.

Issue Title: [webview_flutter] Add Windows support
Requirement: Requirement Statement: The webview_flutter plugin shall be extended to support the Windows platform. This implementation must enable Flutter applications to embed a native Windows webview component, supporting common webview functionalities including page navigation (load, reload, stop), JavaScript execution, and event callbacks (e.g., page load events, error notifications). The solution should integrate with Flutter’s Windows desktop embedding architecture, ensure compatibility with existing Flutter APIs, and include comprehensive testing and documentation specific to Windows.

Issue Title: Support soft hyphenation (line breaks at U+00AD plus rendering a hyphen at the end of the line)
Requirement: Requirement: The framework MUST support soft hyphenation by recognizing the Unicode soft hyphen (U+00AD) in text. When a line break occurs at a location containing a soft hyphen, the system MUST insert a visible hyphen at the end of the line to indicate the break. This feature MUST work across all text rendering contexts in the framework and be configurable where applicable to ensure compatibility with various languages and typography practices.

Issue Title: Reusing state logic is either too verbose or too difficult
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance Flutter’s state management approach to provide a more concise and user-friendly mechanism for reusing state logic. The solution must reduce boilerplate code and complexity when sharing state across widgets while maintaining or improving performance, testability, and compatibility with existing Flutter codebases. It should offer clear guidelines and best practices to aid developers in creating reusable state components that integrate seamlessly with Flutter’s widget lifecycle.

Issue Title: Table > TableRow > TableCell colspan
Requirement: Requirement: Enable TableCell to span multiple columns by introducing a colspan property. The Table widget’s layout logic must be updated to recognize and correctly render cells with a colspan value, ensuring that cells appropriately span across the specified number of columns within a TableRow without disrupting adjacent cell alignments. This functionality should integrate seamlessly with existing Table and TableRow widgets, allow for varying numbers of spans per row, and include unit tests to validate proper layout behavior in different table configurations.

Issue Title: Expo like tool for flutter
Requirement: Requirement: Develop an Expo-like tool for Flutter that simplifies the development process by providing rapid prototyping, streamlined project scaffolding, convenient asset management, and built-in live-reloading and hot reloading capabilities. The tool should support multiple platforms with an emphasis on ease of setup, deployment, and configuration similar to Expo in the React Native ecosystem.

Issue Title: Flutter support for Apple Watch
Requirement: Requirement: Implement Apple Watch support in Flutter to enable the development of native watchOS applications using the Flutter framework. This feature must provide: • A new project template for creating watchOS apps with Flutter. • Integration with watchOS-specific APIs, including UI, notifications, and sensor data. • Seamless communication between the Apple Watch app and its companion iOS app. • Adequate documentation and tooling support for building, debugging, and deploying watchOS applications. • Compatibility with existing Flutter plugins or guidelines for extending them to support watchOS-specific functionalities. • Thorough testing to ensure reliability and performance on various Apple Watch models.

Issue Title: [path_provider] Add support for web
Requirement: Requirement: Extend the flutter/path_provider plugin to support the Web platform by implementing platform-specific APIs for file system path handling, ensuring consistent functionality with existing mobile implementations.

Issue Title: SliverAppBar flexibleSpace with height depending on children
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance the SliverAppBar widget so that its flexibleSpace can dynamically calculate and adjust its height based on the dimensions of its child widgets. This functionality should allow the flexibleSpace to automatically measure its children to determine an appropriate height without requiring a fixed height parameter, while maintaining compatibility with existing scrolling behaviors and layouts in the Flutter framework.

Issue Title: Allow Hero widgets to have transitions within the same screen
Requirement: Requirement: Modify the current Hero widget behavior to support animated transitions between widgets on the same screen. This feature should allow developers to designate parts of the UI that can animate seamlessly from one state to another within a single page, rather than only between different routes or screens. The implementation must ensure that the new functionality maintains consistency with existing Hero animations across route changes while offering a flexible API for intra-screen transitions.

Issue Title: Investigate Swift Package Manager for Swift plugins
Requirement: Requirement: Investigate and assess the integration of Swift Package Manager (SPM) to support Swift plugins within the Flutter framework. The investigation should include: • Reviewing the compatibility of SPM with existing Flutter plugin infrastructure and build processes. • Identifying any required modifications to the plugin development workflow for Swift modules. • Evaluating potential benefits, trade-offs, and performance impacts. • Producing a detailed technical report with proposed action items and documentation updates if SPM integration is deemed beneficial.

Issue Title: Return index of the first visible item in ListView
Requirement: Requirement: The ListView component must expose an API that returns the index of the first fully or partially visible item. This API should update in real-time as the user scrolls, accurately reflecting which item is currently the first visible in the viewport. The API should account for both vertical and horizontal ListView orientations and be accessible via a public method or property for integration in flexible UI scenarios.

Issue Title: Support Firefox as a browser in flutter run
Requirement: Requirement: Add support for Mozilla Firefox as a target browser option within the "flutter run" command to allow users to build, deploy, and test Flutter web applications in Firefox.

Issue Title: [video_player] Support DRM content
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance the flutter video_player plugin to support DRM-protected content. The implementation must include mechanisms to handle encrypted media streams by integrating with DRM license acquisition systems, allowing the plugin to play back DRM content securely. The feature should abstract platform-specific DRM handling (e.g., Widevine on Android, FairPlay on iOS) and provide an API that enables developers to set DRM parameters (such as license URLs, headers, and other necessary credentials). Include proper error handling, API documentation, and testing for both non-DRM and DRM-protected playback scenarios.

Issue Title: [Desktop] - Splash screen or background color customization
Requirement: Requirement: Enable developers to customize the splash screen or background color for desktop applications built with Flutter. This feature should allow specification of a custom color or a splash screen image to be displayed when the application starts, offering configuration options through Flutter’s cross-platform APIs. The solution must be consistent with Flutter’s desktop architecture and be configurable on a per-platform basis.

Issue Title: AVIF codec support
Requirement: Requirement Statement: Integrate AVIF image codec support into Flutter's image processing pipeline to enable decoding and rendering of AVIF images across all supported platforms. This support must adhere to AVIF format specifications, ensuring efficient performance, compatibility with existing image APIs, and seamless integration into the Flutter framework. The implementation should include comprehensive tests (unit and integration) to verify functionality and performance, and provide developers with clear documentation on how to load and manipulate AVIF images within their applications.

Issue Title: Allow release mode builds to run on simulators
Requirement: Requirement: The Flutter tool shall support building release-mode applications that can be deployed and executed within simulator environments (e.g., iOS simulators and compatible Android emulators). In release mode for simulators, the build must incorporate appropriate optimizations to mimic production performance characteristics while accounting for simulator-specific configurations. The solution must maintain compatibility with existing workflows and provide clear documentation for developers on how to generate and run release-mode builds on simulators.

Issue Title: Add structs in GDScript
Requirement: Title: Add Structs Support to GDScript Description:   The GDScript language shall be enhanced with a new "struct" construct allowing developers to define simple, immutable record types. This feature will enable the creation of structured data types that consist of a fixed collection of related fields, similar to records or structs in other programming languages. Requirements:   1. Syntax and Declaration:      a. Include a clear and concise syntax for declaring structs within GDScript.      b. Allow struct declarations to define named fields with specified types, if provided, or inferred types.      c. Support both inline and top-level struct declarations. 2. Immutability and Semantics:      a. Struct instances shall be immutable after creation unless explicitly stated otherwise.      b. Support value-based equality comparison, ensuring that two struct instances with identical values are considered equal. 3. Memory Model and Performance:      a. Ensure that structs are optimized for lightweight, value-type behavior, minimizing runtime overhead.      b. Provide clear semantics on copying and assignment, ensuring that struct instances are passed by value. 4. Integration with GDScript:      a. Ensure that structs integrate seamlessly with existing GDScript features, including functions, arrays, dictionaries, and signals.      b. Enable struct initialization using initializer patterns or constructor-like functions. 5. Tooling and Documentation:      a. Update language documentation to include examples, syntax details, and best practices for using structs.      b. Provide integration in the Godot editor for syntax highlighting, auto-completion, and error checking for structs. 6. Backwards Compatibility:      a. Ensure that introducing structs does not break existing GDScript code.      b. Provide clear migration guidelines or warnings if any potential conflicts with existing idioms occur. Acceptance Criteria:   - Developers can define and use new struct types in GDScript without external dependencies. - Structs support value equality, immutability by default, and efficient copy semantics. - The Godot editor provides proper tooling support for struct syntax. - Documentation and sample code are updated to reflect the new constructs.

Issue Title: Add support for nullable static types in GDScript
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance GDScript’s static type system to support nullable static types. This includes allowing type annotations to indicate that a variable can hold either a specified type or null, updating the language parser and type-checker to recognize nullable annotations, modifying the code generator as needed, and ensuring that error messaging and documentation reflect this change.

Issue Title: Add a Trait system for GDScript
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a trait system for GDScript that allows developers to define reusable sets of functionality (traits) which can be composed into classes. The system should provide a clean syntax for applying multiple traits to a single class, resolve conflicts when traits include methods or properties with similar names, and ensure that traits can access class context if needed. Additionally, the implementation must integrate with existing GDScript language features, maintain performance standards, and include comprehensive documentation and testing to facilitate adoption and further extension by the community.

Issue Title: Allow explicitly defining interfaces in GDScript
Requirement: Requirement: Implement explicit interface definitions in GDScript. The feature must allow developers to declare interfaces, specify their method signatures, and enforce that any GDScript class implementing an interface provides concrete implementations for all of the interface’s methods. Additionally, tooling support (such as code completion and error checking) should be updated to recognize, validate, and index these explicit interface definitions to improve code clarity and maintainability.

Issue Title: Create a Swarm/Mob/Flock/etc system for managing large amounts of entities
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a Swarm Behavior System that efficiently manages and simulates the collective dynamics of a large number of entities. The system must support grouping entities into swarms, mobs, or flocks and provide configurable behaviors such as cohesion, separation, alignment, pathfinding, obstacle avoidance, and emergent group movement. It should be scalable, with optimization for performance in high entity-count scenarios, and easily integrated with existing game objects. Additionally, developers must be able to customize individual and group parameters via an intuitive interface, scripting API, or configuration files to tune behaviors at runtime or during development.

Issue Title: Expose a zero allocation API to Godot C# bindings
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a zero-allocation API extension for Godot’s C# bindings that minimizes or eliminates runtime memory allocations for common operations. This enhancement must: • Offer alternative methods and data handling mechanisms in the C# API that avoid unnecessary allocations during frequent calls. • Be fully compatible with existing Godot C# workflows, ensuring no regressions or incompatibilities. • Provide benchmarks and performance validations to verify reduced memory usage and improved runtime efficiency. • Include thorough documentation and usage examples to assist developers in adopting zero-allocation techniques within their projects.

Issue Title: Add a "Mask2D" node (and/or a "mask_parent" property for Sprite2D)
Requirement: Requirement: Introduce a masking functionality for 2D scenes by implementing a dedicated "Mask2D" node and an optional "mask_parent" property for the Sprite2D node. The "Mask2D" node should define a region that other 2D nodes (e.g., Sprite2D, CanvasItem-based nodes) can use to limit their visible area. When a node specifies a "mask_parent" property referencing a "Mask2D" node, its rendering should be clipped to the mask region defined by that node. The implementation must support dynamic modifications to the mask, allowing real-time updates to the visible areas as the mask changes shape or position. Ensure compatibility with Godot's existing 2D rendering pipeline and provide documentation, usage examples, and tests demonstrating the integration of masking via both the dedicated node and property-based approaches.

Issue Title: Add support for multiple displays/screens/monitors in Godot editor
Requirement: The Godot editor shall support multi-display setups by allowing users to extend, detach, and position floating panels and windows across multiple monitors. This support must include the ability for users to customize and save window layouts spanning multiple displays, detect connected displays, and manage primary versus secondary monitor behavior. Additionally, the feature should enable seamless integration of multi-monitor setups during runtime and provide configuration options for display-specific scaling and positioning to ensure an optimal editing experience in diverse hardware environments.

Issue Title: Add union types to Typed GDScript
Requirement: Requirement ID: GDTPRO-UT01 Title: Implement Union Types in Typed GDScript Description: Extend the Typed GDScript language to support union types, allowing variables, function parameters, and return types to accept multiple specified types. The implementation should include: • Syntax support for union type declarations (e.g., type1 | type2). • Updated type-checking mechanisms to account for union types during compile-time verification. • Error messaging that clearly indicates incompatibility when values do not match any member type in the union. • Documentation updates and examples demonstrating the usage and best practices of union types. Acceptance Criteria: 1. Union types can be declared and used in variable declarations, function signatures, and type annotations. 2. The type checker accepts values matching any of the types specified in the union and reports errors for mismatches. 3. Performance impact of union type checking does not degrade script compilation time beyond acceptable thresholds. 4. Documentation and tests are updated to cover union types use cases. Dependencies: Coordination with the Typed GDScript language design team and updates to the GDScript parser, type checker, and documentation.

Issue Title: Add "refactor" tooling to rename symbols in the script editor
Requirement: Title: Implement Refactor-Rename Tool in the Script Editor Requirement: The system shall provide a refactoring tool in the script editor that enables users to rename symbols (such as variables, functions, classes, etc.) across a project safely and consistently. The tool must: • Scan and identify all occurrences of the symbol within the current script and across project files. • Offer a preview of all changes prior to applying modifications. • Detect potential conflicts or errors resulting from the rename operation and alert the user. • Integrate seamlessly with the existing UI of the script editor, following current design guidelines. • Support undo/redo operations for changes made by the refactoring tool. • Be extensible to support additional refactoring operations in future updates.

Issue Title: Add public/private access modifiers to GDScript and autocompletion improvements
Requirement: Requirement Statement: The system shall enhance GDScript by introducing explicit public and private access modifiers for class member variables and functions. Specifically, members marked as private must only be accessible within their defining class, ensuring proper encapsulation, while public members remain accessible externally as before. In addition, the integrated development environment (IDE) must be updated to provide contextual autocompletion that respects these modifiers, accurately suggesting only accessible members based on the current scope and reflecting the new access control semantics.

Issue Title: Add support for global plugins/universal addons
Requirement: The system shall provide a global plugin framework that allows plugins or add-ons to be installed, managed, and activated independently of individual project directories. Global plugins must be stored in a common location and be discoverable by any project, with options to enable or disable them on a per-project basis. The framework must include mechanisms for version management, conflict resolution, and security to ensure that global plugins integrate seamlessly with the project environment while maintaining consistent behavior across all projects.

Issue Title: Implement a Rendering Compositor
Requirement: Implement a Rendering Compositor that integrates into the existing Godot rendering pipeline, allowing users to define, configure, and dynamically adjust multi-layered rendering workflows. The feature must support: • Customizable compositing operations, including blend modes, multi-pass effects, and the ability to combine outputs from multiple sources (e.g., cameras, viewports, buffers). • A user-accessible API and editor tools that enable designers to visually configure and modify the render layers and their interactions at runtime. • Extensibility to incorporate custom post-processing effects and to seamlessly integrate with existing and future rendering features. • Performance optimizations that ensure minimal overhead, maintaining real-time rendering capabilities across supported platforms. • Comprehensive documentation and sample configurations to facilitate adoption and customization by the community.

Issue Title: Replace GridMap with an improved TileMap3D node (inspired by the new 2D TileMap)
Requirement: Requirement: Develop an improved TileMap3D node that replaces the current GridMap system. The enhanced node must draw inspiration from the 2D TileMap by incorporating features such as easier tile editing, efficient performance for 3D tile-based level design, a more intuitive workflow for artists and designers, support for multiple layers, collision integration, flexible tile transformations, and robust tooling for real-time editing and visualization in the 3D scene view. The implementation should maintain compatibility with existing projects, provide a smooth migration path from GridMap to the new TileMap3D node, and include comprehensive documentation and sample projects demonstrating its use.

Issue Title: Add array unpacking/destructuring to GDScript
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance GDScript by implementing array unpacking (destructuring) functionality that allows developers to assign multiple variables from an array’s contents in a single statement. The feature must support basic destructuring patterns (e.g., assigning individual array elements to separate variables), including cases of nested arrays, and enable partial unpacking when the number of target variables is fewer than the array elements. It should provide clear syntax rules, consistent error handling for mismatches in the number or type of elements, and maintain backward compatibility with existing GDScript code.

Issue Title: Calinou doesn't sleep
Requirement: Requirement: Implement an idle behavior for Calinou in which, after a configurable period of inactivity, the character automatically transitions into a sleeping animation state. The feature must include settings that allow users to customize the inactivity timeout duration and enable or disable this behavior. Additionally, the implementation should ensure that Calinou's sleep state interrupts ongoing interactions seamlessly and that any exit from the sleep state (triggered by user input or other relevant events) is smooth and contextually appropriate.

Issue Title: Add proper and complete support for multi-pass shaders
Requirement: Requirement: The engine shall provide complete support for multi-pass shaders, enabling developers to define, compile, and execute shaders with multiple rendering passes within a single shader program. This feature must include:  1. Syntax and API extensions to allow specifying multiple shader passes, with clear and consistent semantics. 2. Automatic management of rendering state transitions between passes, including blending modes, depth settings, and culling rules. 3. Compatibility with existing single-pass shaders, ensuring that legacy projects remain functional without modifications. 4. Performance optimizations to minimize overhead introduced by multi-pass processing. 5. Comprehensive documentation and example projects demonstrating multi-pass shader workflows in various rendering contexts.

Issue Title: Godot C# GDExtension Roadmap Discussion
Requirement: Requirement Statement: Develop a comprehensive, publicly accessible roadmap specifically for the Godot C# GDExtension implementation to guide the evolution and migration from the current C# modules to the new GDExtension system. The roadmap must include clear milestones, timeline estimates, required feature parity analyses with existing functionality, performance targets, backward compatibility considerations, migration guidelines, and community feedback integration mechanisms to ensure alignment with the broader Godot engine evolution.

Issue Title: Add literal quoted strings with embedded variables (f-strings) to GDScript
Requirement: Title: Support for f-string style literal quoted strings with embedded variables in GDScript Requirement: GDScript shall be extended to include a new string literal format similar to Python’s f-strings. Developers must be able to embed variable references and simple expressions directly within quoted string literals using a designated syntax (e.g., prefixing the string with a special marker such as "f" and delimiting embedded expressions with curly braces {}). Acceptance Criteria: 1. String literals prefixed with an f-designator (or equivalent) are recognized by the parser, allowing embedded expressions within curly braces. 2. Embedded expressions are evaluated at runtime and their results interpolated into the final string. 3. Error diagnostics are provided at compile-time for invalid embedded expressions or syntax errors. 4. The feature is fully integrated with existing GDScript tooling (syntax highlighting, debugging, etc.) and is documented in the official language reference. 5. Edge cases such as escaping delimiters and nested braces are handled consistently with established language patterns.

Issue Title: Implement Terrain
Requirement: Title: Implement Terrain System in Godot Engine Requirement Statement: The Godot Engine shall include a dedicated, high-performance terrain system that enables developers to generate and manipulate large-scale 3D landscapes. This terrain system shall support real-time rendering with level of detail (LOD) management for efficient performance, dynamic streaming of terrain data, and integration with physics for collision handling. Additionally, the system shall provide intuitive in-editor tools for terrain sculpting, heightmap editing, texturing, and placement of detail objects, ensuring seamless workflow for both prototyping and production use. The terrain system must be extensible with customizable shaders and support integration with existing Godot modules such as lighting and particle systems.

Issue Title: Improve the performance of the GDScript VM
Requirement: The system shall improve the performance of the GDScript virtual machine by implementing optimizations that reduce execution overhead, enhance instruction dispatch efficiency, and lower memory usage. These optimizations must target critical execution paths such as function calls, loops, and frequently executed operations while maintaining compatibility across all supported platforms and ensuring that debugging and error-reporting functionalities remain intact.

Issue Title: Add procedural and parametrizable audio support
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a procedural audio system with parameterizable controls in Godot. The system must allow developers to generate audio content dynamically at runtime using configurable parameters (such as frequency, amplitude, modulation, and effects parameters) and provide an API to control and modify these parameters in real time. The implementation should support a range of use cases, including gameplay sound effects, music synthesis, and adaptive soundscapes, while ensuring high performance and low latency in audio generation and processing.

Issue Title: Rework the Tilemap terrain system to improve its usability
Requirement: Requirement: Redesign and implement the Tilemap terrain system in Godot to improve its usability by introducing an intuitive interface for terrain editing, simplified workflow for terrain shape creation and modification, real-time visual feedback during editing, and robust support for various terrain configurations. The new system must integrate seamlessly with existing Tilemap workflows, support both simple and complex terrain designs, and include comprehensive documentation and sample projects to aid users in learning and adopting the new terrain editing features.

Issue Title: Implement namespaces in GDScript
Requirement: Requirement: Implement Namespace Support in GDScript The GDScript language shall be extended to support namespaces, allowing users to organize code into distinct hierarchical scopes. This includes: • Syntax and semantics for declaring a namespace in a script. • Mechanisms for importing and referencing namespaced symbols (functions, variables, classes, etc.) to avoid naming conflicts. • Compiler enhancements to enforce namespace scoping rules. • Updates to documentation, examples, and possibly an integrated tool to refactor existing code into namespaces.

Issue Title: Add WebGPU support
Requirement: Requirement: Implement support for WebGPU in the Godot engine by integrating the WebGPU API to enable hardware-accelerated modern graphics rendering and compute operations on web platforms. This support should include adapting the rendering pipeline for WebGPU compatibility, providing necessary abstractions for shader and resource management, ensuring fallbacks or compatibility options for environments without WebGPU, and offering documentation and example projects to facilitate developer adoption and testing.

Issue Title: Obfuscate GDScript in production export
Requirement: Requirement: In production exports, enable an option to obfuscate GDScript source code to help protect intellectual property. When enabled, the build process should transform the GDScript code into an obfuscated version that retains identical runtime behavior and performance. The obfuscation process should be integrated into the export pipeline, configurable by the user through the export settings, and reversible only through debugging symbols/log files to support crash reporting without exposing the original source code.

Issue Title: Implement a Set primitive to complement Dictionary and Array
Requirement: Requirement: Add a native Set data type to the engine that functions as an unordered collection of unique elements. The Set shall provide an API similar to existing Array and Dictionary types and include operations such as insertion, deletion, membership testing, union, intersection, difference, and iteration. The implementation should ensure efficient performance comparable to or better than current data types and integrate seamlessly with the scripting language and engine systems.

Issue Title: Implement a code formatter for GDScript in the script editor
Requirement: Requirement: Develop and integrate a GDScript code formatter within Godot's script editor. The formatter must automatically indent and align code, enforce configurable style guidelines (such as line length, spacing, and bracket/colon placement), support common formatting actions (e.g., on-save formatting and manual trigger via command), provide real-time preview of formatting changes, and allow users to customize or disable rules as necessary through settings. The implementation should target consistent output to improve code readability and adhere to best practices for GDScript.

Issue Title: Implement method overloading in GDScript
Requirement: Title: Implement Method Overloading in GDScript Requirement Statement: GDScript shall support method overloading, allowing multiple functions with the same name to coexist within the same scope, differentiated by the number and/or types of parameters. The language compiler must resolve and bind the appropriate function call at compile-time based on the provided arguments. In cases of ambiguity—where multiple overloads could match—or when no matching overload exists, clear and descriptive error messages must be generated. This implementation must be fully backward compatible with existing GDScript code, and comprehensive updates to the language documentation are required, including detailed examples, usage guidelines, and potential limitations of the method overloading feature.

Issue Title: Add support for variadic functions (varargs) to GDScript
Requirement: Requirement: Extend GDScript to support variadic functions, allowing developers to define functions that accept a variable number of arguments. The implementation must introduce a clear and intuitive syntax (e.g., using a designated "varargs" operator such as args) so that parameters captured in this way are accessible as an array within the function body. The feature must include comprehensive error handling for incorrect use, maintain backwards compatibility with existing function definitions, and be documented with updated language references and example usages.

Issue Title: rustdoc support for per-parameter documentation
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance rustdoc to allow documentation for individual function parameters. The implementation must enable authors to specify documentation for each parameter directly within the function signature (or associated documentation block) and have these descriptions rendered in the generated documentation. This functionality should support consistent formatting with existing rustdoc outputs and maintain compatibility with documentation tests and tooling.

Issue Title: Linking with LLD
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance the Rust compiler's linker interface to support integration with the LLVM linker (LLD) as an alternative to the default system linker. This should include detection of LLD availability, proper command-line argument conversion for compatibility, handling of platform-specific behavior, and clear error messaging when linking fails with LLD. The feature should be configurable via a compiler flag or environment variable, allowing users to opt-in for LLD linkage.

Issue Title: A new compiler flag: "link everything statically or die, dammit!"
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a new compiler flag (e.g., -C link-static-all) that enforces complete static linking during the compilation process. When this flag is enabled, the compiler must verify that every required library and dependency is linked statically. If any component would result in dynamic linking, compilation should fail with a clear, descriptive error message. The implementation must include updates to the compiler’s command-line interface, documented behavior in the user manual, and comprehensive testing to ensure that the flag consistently enforces static linking across all relevant platforms and scenarios.

Issue Title: Need negative trait bound
Requirement: Requirement: The rustc compiler shall support negative trait bounds, allowing type parameters to specify that a type does not implement a certain trait (e.g., T: !Trait). This feature must integrate with existing trait bound syntax, provide clear compile-time error messages when violations occur, and include appropriate tests to ensure consistency and correctness with respect to trait resolution and object safety.

Issue Title: Crate local state for procedural macros?
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a crate-local state mechanism for procedural macros that allows them to define and maintain state scoped to a single crate. This mechanism should enable procedural macros to store and retrieve state data across macro invocations within the same crate without exposing or interfering with global state. The design must ensure memory safety, thread-safety (if applicable), and should integrate seamlessly with the existing procedural macro infrastructure without adversely affecting compile-time performance.

Issue Title: Include images in rustdoc output
Requirement: The documentation generator, rustdoc, shall support the inclusion and proper rendering of images referenced within documentation comments. When an image is specified using standard markdown image syntax (e.g., ![alt text](path/to/image.png)), rustdoc shall locate the image file (supporting both relative and absolute paths) and embed it into the generated HTML output. The implementation must handle missing or broken image references gracefully, providing an informative warning during the documentation build process without halting generation. Additionally, rustdoc should ensure that images are displayed responsively across various devices and do not negatively impact page load performance.

Issue Title: Using std::io::{Read, Write, Cursor} in a nostd environment
Requirement: Requirement: Enable support for no_std environments by providing no_std-compatible implementations of std::io::Read, std::io::Write, and std::io::Cursor, allowing users to perform I/O operations without depending on the full standard library.

Issue Title: Provide a means of turning iterators into fixed-size arrays
Requirement: Requirement: Provide a standard library feature that enables converting an iterator to a fixed-size array. This feature should include an API that takes an iterator and returns an array of a specified fixed length, handling cases where the iterator may not produce exactly the required number of elements. The API must: • Validate that the iterator produces exactly the required number of elements before performing the conversion and return an appropriate error or panic if the count is incorrect. • Be generic over element types, enabling conversion for any indexable type that satisfies the fixed-size array requirements. • Efficiently implement the conversion with minimal overhead and support compile-time checks where applicable. • Include clear documentation, examples, and tests to guide users and ensure correctness. This feature should be designed to integrate with existing iterator traits and be accessible as a stable, well-documented method or trait extension in the standard library.

Issue Title: Add function to make paths absolute, which is different from canonicalization
Requirement: Requirement: Implement a function that accepts a file system path and returns its absolute representation. The conversion should be performed by prefixing the path with the current working directory (or a provided base directory) when necessary, without resolving symbolic links or verifying file existence. This behavior differs from canonicalization, which typically resolves symbolic links and normalizes the path by actually querying the file system.

Issue Title: Proc macros: ability to refer to a specific crate/symbol (something similar to `$crate`)
Requirement: Requirement Title: Proc Macro Explicit Crate and Symbol Resolution Requirement Statement: The system shall provide a mechanism for procedural macros that enables referencing specific crates or symbols similarly to the $crate syntax used in macro_rules!. This capability must allow a proc macro to explicitly refer to a designated crate instance or symbol, ensuring correct symbol resolution even when multiple crate versions or renamings are in use. The solution should include syntax for specifying an exact crate/symbol target, integration with the compiler’s resolution and linking phases, and thorough handling of edge cases such as version conflicts or renames documented in the crate manifest.

Issue Title: Inclusive version of take_while
Requirement: Requirement: Introduce a new iterator adaptor method, take_while_inclusive, for the standard iterator trait, which functions similarly to take_while but includes the first element that does not satisfy the provided predicate. This method should work seamlessly with existing iterator chains, maintain performance characteristics consistent with current iterator adaptors, and include documentation and tests demonstrating its behavior with edge cases (e.g., an empty iterator, all elements satisfying the predicate, and the first element failing the predicate).

Issue Title: Initializing array of Option<T> using [None; n] syntax should not require std::marker::Copy for T
Requirement: The system SHALL allow arrays of Option<T> to be initialized using the [None n] syntax without requiring T to implement the std::marker::Copy trait. Specifically, the implementation of the [None n] syntax for initializing arrays must be modified so that it does not impose a Copy requirement on T when constructing Option<T> values, enabling the use case where T is non‑Copy.

Issue Title: Add ability to ignore tests at runtime.
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance the Rust test runner to support ignoring specified tests at runtime. The implementation should allow developers to mark tests for runtime exclusion via a command-line flag or configuration setting, ensuring that such tests are skipped during execution while still being reported in the test summary. The functionality must integrate smoothly with existing test filtering mechanisms and include corresponding documentation and tests to validate proper behavior.

Issue Title: Add Vec::contains_ref which is worse for inference but less restrictive than Vec::contains
Requirement: Requirement: Add a new Vec method named contains_ref to the Rust standard library. This method should take a reference to an element and determine if an equivalent element exists in the Vec by comparing via PartialEq. Unlike the existing contains method, contains_ref should accept a parameter with a different type from the Vec’s element type if a valid equality comparison exists (i.e., supporting more flexible type inference and coercion scenarios). The implementation must clearly document the trade-offs regarding type inference limitations compared to contains and specify its less restrictive matching behavior.

Issue Title: Feature request: Use 'trampolines' to make most of the body of a generic function non-generic
Requirement: Requirement: Enhance the Rust compiler by implementing "trampolines" that allow most of a generic function’s body to be compiled as non-generic code, reducing per-instantiation overhead. The implementation must: • Identify and separate the parts of generic functions that do not depend on type parameters from those that do. • Generate a small, type-specialized “trampoline” section that forwards calls to a shared, non-generic implementation for the function’s body. • Ensure that this transformation preserves type safety, correctness, and all existing language semantics, including lifetimes and trait constraints. • Provide a mechanism (e.g., via compiler flags or internal heuristics) to control the application of this optimization. • Maintain interoperability with existing optimization and code generation pipelines. This feature will improve compilation and runtime performance for generic functions by reducing code duplication without compromising language functionality.

Issue Title: Subslice search
Requirement: Requirement: Extend the Rust standard library by adding subslice search functionality for slices. Specifically, provide a set of safe, efficient, and ergonomic API methods (e.g., find_subslice and contains_subslice) that allow users to search for a contiguous sequence (subslice) within a larger slice.
